correctness.rationale: PASS. For opposite corners of a simple four-cycle in the ambient transposition Cayley graph, their two-step difference is either a three-cycle or a product of disjoint transpositions. The first forms a K_(3,3) parity-coset on a unique set of three positions; retaining derangements yields precisely 9 squares when zero positions intersect the image set, 1 when one intersects, and none when at least two intersect. The outside partial permutation count is the explicitly specified diagonal-avoidance B0/B1. Two commuting disjoint transpositions produce a unique square on four positions; all four corners avoid the diagonal exactly when the matching permutation avoids a pair of 2x2 forbidden rook boards with polynomial (1+4x+2x²)²(1+x)^(n-4). Each such square has four possible starting corners, establishing the factor 1/4. The degree identity deg(pi)=binom(n,2)-n+c2(pi), exact one- and two-selected 2-cycle sums and elementary closed-four-walk partition prove the fourth moment. Independent code reconstructed the graph directly and computed all square types and tr(A^4) for n=4,5,6; results (Q3,Q4,trA4)=(0,3,144),(60,60,3360),(1800,1305,70560) agree. Finite enumeration is corroboration, not the proof for n>6.
